_comment: English. Translated FROM locales/hi-Latn/guided.json, which is the field-tested reference. Strings that name a control on another screen -- 'Router Fleet', 'Download .rsc', 'Generate', 'Rotate the RouterOS API password', 'API Access', 'WinBox Terminal', 'cloudguest-api', '.rsc' -- are byte-identical across all three bundles because the Master console generator is English-only and the operator matches those labels by eye.
lang.label: Language
shell.title: Guided Setup — {{router}}
shell.noPhases: No setup phases have loaded yet.
shell.resetConfirm: This router's guided progress will be erased (every answer you gave). Nothing on the router itself changes. Reset?
shell.finishedBody: Every phase is done. Guests can now sign in on this router and get online. If something breaks later, go straight to the "{{recovery}}" phase.
phase.rscDownloaded: Downloaded a .rsc of this phase's commands
phase.reRunnable: same on every router · safe to re-run
phase.copyProvesNothing: Copied does not mean it ran on the router. The checks below are the only real proof.
phase.gateOpen: All clear -- you can move on
phase.gateHint: Every check has to read "{{pass}}" or "{{warning}}".
check.fixHeading: To fix it -- do the one whose case matches:
check.afterFix: After the fix, run the step above again and paste the new output.
check.noFix: There is no ready-made fix for this check -- look it up in diagnostics.
check.openDiagnostics: None of these match -- open diagnostics
copy.failed: Copy failed -- select it below and copy manually.
copy.done: Copied -- now paste it into WinBox Terminal
diag.title: What are you seeing?
diag.placeholder: Type what you saw on screen -- e.g. 'spinner stuck' or 'certificate warning'
diag.noMatch: Nothing matched this filter -- click "{{all}}" and look again.
generated.heading: First: paste this chunk from the Master console
generated.body: These parts belong to this router alone (IDs, keys, secrets) -- they cannot be shown here. Open the Master console, generate the script, then copy the chunks named below and paste them on the router. Only after that run this page's universal blocks.
generated.secretsOnce: These secrets are shown only once
generated.secretsBody: The WireGuard key, the RADIUS secret and the API password cannot be retrieved again. "Download .rsc" in the Master console is your only real copy -- do not close that tab before you have it.
generated.step9Note: Coming here after the step 9 cleanup? In the Master console also tick the "Rotate the RouterOS API password" box -- otherwise the "API Access" chunk will not appear in the script at all and the router's cloudguest-api user will never come back. In a normal setup, leave that box alone.
generated.ack: I have a copy -- downloaded the .rsc or saved it somewhere safe.
generated.nonSecretNote: Press "Download .rsc" in the Master console to keep a copy of the whole script -- it also holds the later phases' secrets, which are never shown again.
regen.trigger: Do you need to press "Generate" again in the Master console? Read this first.
regen.heading: Stop -- pressing Generate again kills the router silently
regen.p1: The moment you press Generate, a new WireGuard key and a new RADIUS secret are created on the server. The router keeps the old ones, because the script is written in a "if it already exists, leave it alone" style.
regen.p2: The result: the tunnel and guest login both stop, and the router shows no error at all. Pasting every chunk again does not fix it either. The old secrets have to be removed from the router first.
regen.typeName: To continue, type the router's name:
regen.tail: Phase 9 first checks whether there really is a secret mismatch, then resets only the secrets -- the rest of the router's setup survives. Only after that should you press Generate again, and in that Generate tick the "Rotate the RouterOS API password" box.

check.redacted: {{count}} secret value(s) removed ({{keys}}) -- only the redacted text is kept in the app.
check.columnSecret: This table may have a secret column the app could not cut out safely. Do not copy it anywhere else -- run `print detail` and paste that output instead.
check.overrideUnknown: The app could not verify it -- I checked myself, it is fine
check.unverifiable: The app cannot verify this step. It produces no router output that can be read -- this one is on your eyes only. What you tick below is your own confirmation, not the app's.
